newsitem.title: USA: Tower, A.O. Smith shares up on deal.
newsitem.headline: Tower, A.O. Smith shares up on deal.

text.p: Shares of Tower Automotive Inc and A.O. Smith Corp were both higher Monday afternoon on benefits both companies will reap after Tower's purchase of A.O. Smith's Automotive Products division for $625 million, industry analysts said.

"This makes excellent strategic sense for Tower," said Greg Konezny, an analyst at Piper Jaffray Inc. "Tower makes the internal structural supports for automobiles, and A.O. Smith makes spring systems, engine mounts and suspensions."
Tower shares were up 2-7/8 at 36-7/8, while A.O. Smith shares were up 3-3/4 at 33-3/4.
"Once this deal closes," Konezny added, "Tower will make every component of an automobile chassis except for the sheet metal exterior panels."

"This (deal) will be accretive to Tower's earnings per share in 1997 and enhance Tower's operations," Kari Montanus, an analyst at Morgan Stanley & Co, said. "It could add between $0.20 and $0.30 a share, maybe higher."
Tower reported sales of $114.6 million in the third quarter and sales for the nine months that ended September 30 of $280.0 million.
A.O. Smith's automotive unit posted annual sales of $860 million in 1996.

"With the proceeds of this deal, A.O. Smith can now pay off its debt load of about $200 million and still have some cash to pay for the various projects its scientists are working on," said Allen Roness, an analyst at JW Charles Securities.
James Hilgert, an analyst Stifel Nicolaus & Co, said A.O. Smith wanted to refocus on its storage tanks and fiberglass pipeline operations.

"A.O. Smith had something going (with the automotive products operation)," Hilgert said, "but it apparently didn't want to make the investment necessary to supply global manufacturers on a just-in-time basis."
Piper Jaffray's Konezny also believes growth opportunities are also on the horizon for Tower.
"I think we'll see the European component come into play as a factor in the company's future growth," he said.
